description: احنا فريق مكون شخصين من مصر بنحب بلدنا. مشروعنا بيخلى القمر يراقب السيل والطلمبات تشتغل لوحدها قبل الخطر.
summary: Project Flood Guards protects Sinai from destructive flash floods and turns flood water into a resource for agriculture. We use NASA GPM-IMERG data to monitor rainfall every 30 minutes and NASA Giovanni to map rainfall over Sinai. When rainfall exceeds a safe level, our system sends an early warning to residents and automatically opens smart underground tanks to collect flood water. The stored water is then filtered and used to irrigate olive trees and palm trees, which are famous in Sinai. In the 2010 Wadi El-Arish flood, 780 houses were destroyed and 1076 houses were flooded. Our project aims to prevent this damage, protect lives and homes, and provide water for farming in a dry region.
details: > *What does it do?* > Project Flood Guards is an early warning and water harvesting system for Sinai. It uses NASA GPM-IMERG satellite data to monitor rainfall every 30 minutes. When rain reaches a dangerous level, the system sends an alert to people in El-Arish, Sheikh Zuweid and Central Sinai, and automatically opens smart underground tanks to collect flood water before it destroys houses. > > *How does it work?* > 1. NASA GPM satellite measures rainfall over Sinai. > 2. NASA Giovanni is used to map and analyze rainfall. > 3. NASA SRTM data shows mountains and valleys to know where the flood will go. > 4. A water sensor opens the tank automatically when the flood arrives. > 5. The stored water is filtered and used for farming olive trees and palm trees. > > *Benefits:* > Protects houses and lives, reduces damage that cost 25.3 million dollars in the 2010 flood, and provides water for agriculture in a dry area. > > *Innovation:* > We don't just warn people, we turn the danger into a benefit. Flood water becomes farm water. > > *Tools used:* > NASA GPM-IMERG, NASA Giovanni, NASA SRTM, Google Earth, Canva for design.
